keys.unit: a 1 km cell of the national grid (EPSG:3035)
keys.class: 1 village, 2 suburban, 3 terraced, 4 apartment blocks, 5 dense fabric: lower bounds 0, 250, 1500, 6000, 12000 by the census population count of the cell (twin/globe classes.json)
keys.blocks: 50 km squares; hold-out by three of six contiguous bands, seed 20261113

envelope.population: private households; communal accommodation is outside it
envelope.key: the density of a 1 km tile as this census counts it, not as the twin's population grid does
envelope.classes_resolved: village, suburban, terraced by block count; apartment blocks and dense fabric are unresolved (effective blocks 25 and 8) and their rows are readings only

budgets.whose: the campaign author's, stated before any file was read

law: each row's shares sum to 1,000,000 within 4 parts; the village row is published as 1, 2, 3 and 4-or-more because its 5 and 6+ columns failed the disclosure check
checker: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('household_table.json'));assert all(abs(sum(r['shares_ppm'])-10**6)<=4 for r in d['rows'].values())"

limits: counts are perturbed by a cell-key method; in village cells every size column is 1.4 to 5.4 % below the 10 km file and the residual mean of the 6+ band reads 9.5 where 6 to 8 is possible
households are partly constructed by the census (one per occupied dwelling; unmatched register persons placed by statistical criteria)
household size and building size are two margins; no joint is published
the building reading has no generator scored against it
holds_no_real_feature: This table holds no coordinate, cell id, name or tag of any real place. It holds rows of counts and shares by class.
